Quotations 97–120 of 696.

  1. The secret of happiness is this: let your interests be as wide as possible, and let your reactions…be as far as possible friendly rather than hostile.
    Bertrand Russell
    Happiness
  2. To abandon the struggle for private happiness…to burn with passion for eternal things — this is emancipation.
    Bertrand Russell
    Philosophy
  3. The art of progress is to preserve order amid change, and to preserve change amid order.
    Alfred North Whitehead
    Philosophy
  4. Any man can err; only a fool persists in error.
    Cicero
    Philosophy
  5. Do not seek for things to happen as you wish, but wish for things to happen as they do, and you will flow well.
    Epictetus
    Philosophy
  6. What is not good for the hive is not good for the bee.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Community
  7. Man is a sacred thing to man.
    Seneca
    Dignity
  8. Virtue does not come from money, but from virtue come money and all other good things for human beings.
    Socrates
    Virtue
  9. We become just by doing just acts, temperate by doing temperate acts.
    Aristotle
    Habit
  10. Nature's wealth has its bounds and is easy to procure; but the wealth of vain fancies recedes to an infinite distance.
    Epicurus
    Desire
  11. It is impossible to think of anything at all in the world, or indeed even beyond it, that could be considered good without limitation except a good will.
    Immanuel Kant
    Freedom
  12. There are more things to admire in men than to despise.
    Albert Camus
    Humanity
  13. To will oneself free is also to will others free.
    Simone de Beauvoir
    Freedom
  14. Believe that life is worth living, and your belief will help create the fact.
    William James
    Knowledge
  15. A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds.
    Ralph Waldo Emerson
    Authenticity
  16. One must still have chaos in oneself to be able to give birth to a dancing star.
    Friedrich Nietzsche
    Creation
  17. Depart then in peace; the one who releases you is also at peace.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Death
  18. The usefulness of living is not in length of days, but in their use: one may have lived long, and yet have lived little.
    Michel de Montaigne
    Life
  19. To know, in order to foresee, so as to be able to act.
    Auguste Comte
    Knowledge
  20. Reading means thinking with someone else's head instead of one's own.
    Arthur Schopenhauer
    Philosophy
  21. Solitude is the lot of all outstanding minds.
    Arthur Schopenhauer
    Philosophy
  22. Marry, and you will regret it; do not marry, and you will also regret it.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Choice
  23. Despair is not to will to be oneself — or else to will to be oneself.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Philosophy
  24. Truth happens to an idea. It becomes true, is made true by events.
    William James
    Truth
